proposals.before: Chapter 64a: Biographies of Yan Zhu, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, Yan An, Zhong Jun, Wang Bao, and Jia Yi (part one).
proposals.after: Chapter 64a: Biographies of Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, Yan An, Zhong Jun, Wang Bao, and Jia Yi (part one).
proposals.reason: Chinese title enumerates 朱 after 嚴; the idiomatic list omits Zhu Maichen while naming the other biographees.

proposals.before: When the king of Nanhai rose in revolt, your late servant's father sent General Jian Ji against him; the rebels yielded and were resettled on the Shanggan river.
proposals.after: When the king of Nanhai rose in revolt, Your Majesty's former subject sent General Jian Ji against him; the rebels yielded and were resettled on the Shanggan river.
proposals.reason: Chinese 陛下先臣 means Your Majesty's former/late subject, not "your late servant's father"; the idiomatic invents a father relationship absent from the source.

proposals.before: In my humble view, a wholesale bow ban would do more harm than good."
proposals.after: In my humble view, forbidding the people to carry bows and crossbows would be expedient.
proposals.reason: Chinese 禁民毋得挾弓弩便 states the ban is convenient/beneficial; the idiomatic reverses this into "more harm than good."

proposals.before: Dwelling one month, the wife hanged herself; Maichen begged money from her husband, ordered burial.
proposals.after: Dwelling one month, the wife hanged herself; Maichen gave money for her husband and ordered burial.
proposals.reason: 乞其夫錢 means providing/requesting funds for the husband's burial of the wife, not begging money from the husband.

proposals.before: their herdsmen cannot be ruled from Xianyang.
proposals.after: their people cannot be tamed and guarded.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'from Xianyang', absent from Chinese 得其民，不可調而守也.

proposals.before: Because no feudal lord seemed worth serving, in the first year of Yuanguang he entered the passes to see the General of Wei.
proposals.after: Because no feudal lord seemed worth serving, in the first year of Yuanguang he entered the passes to see General Wei.
proposals.reason: 衛將軍 is General Wei (title of Wei Qing), not 'the General of Wei'.

proposals.before: The General of Wei repeatedly spoke of him to the Emperor, but the Emperor did not take notice.
proposals.after: General Wei repeatedly spoke of him to the Emperor, but the Emperor did not take notice.
proposals.reason: 衛將軍 should be rendered 'General Wei', not 'the General of Wei'.

proposals.before: He had a hand in raising Empress Wei and in unmasking the crimes of Liu Dingguo, king of Yan.
proposals.after: He had a hand in raising Empress Wei and in unmasking the crimes of Dingguo, king of Yan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 燕王定國 does not give the surname Liu; idiomatic invents 'Liu Dingguo'.

proposals.before: The King of Zhao feared he would become the state's calamity, wished to submit a memorial speaking his secret affairs, but because Yan dwelt at the center, did not dare send it.
proposals.after: The King of Zhao feared he would become the state's calamity, wished to submit a memorial speaking of his (Zhufu Yan's) secret affairs, but because Yan dwelt at the center, did not dare send it.
proposals.reason: 言其陰事 refers to Zhufu Yan's secret affairs; the literal 'speaking his secret affairs' wrongly points the pronoun at Zhao.

decisions.reason: Title 嚴朱吾丘主父徐嚴終王賈 lists 朱 after 嚴; Yan Zhu (嚴助) is not that 朱, so omitting Zhu Maichen is a real omission and the repair restores him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 嚴朱吾丘主父徐嚴終王賈傳

decisions.after: When the king of Nanhai rose in revolt, your late subject, my father, sent General Jian Ji against him; the rebels yielded and were resettled on the Shanggan river.
decisions.reason: The traditional commentary identifies 先臣 as Liu An's deceased father, Liu Chang. The original garbles that relationship, while the proposal loses the useful identification entirely.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 陛下先臣使將軍間忌將兵擊之

decisions.after: In my humble view, forbidding the people to carry bows and crossbows would be expedient."
decisions.reason: 便 affirms the ban is expedient; 'more harm than good' reverses the Chinese. The proposal is right on meaning but drops the closing quotation mark that ends the speech.

decisions.after: After a month, the wife hanged herself; Maichen gave her husband money and had him bury her.
decisions.reason: 乞其夫錢 here is Maichen supplying money to the husband for burial, not begging from him; the proposal fixes direction but 'gave money for her husband' is awkward English.

decisions.after: Even if their people were obtained, they could not be governed and held.
decisions.reason: Source is 得其民，不可調而守也; 'from Xianyang' and 'herdsmen' are not in the Chinese, and the proposed wording restores people and 調而守.
衛將軍 is Wei Qing's title General Wei; 'the General of Wei' wrongly suggests a territorial office and should be corrected.
Same title 衛將軍; rendering it 'General Wei' matches the Chinese and avoids the misleading 'of Wei'.
The King Dingguo of Yan was Liu Dingguo. Supplying his surname is an accurate and useful clarification, not a fidelity error.

decisions.after: The King of Zhao feared that Yan would become a calamity to his state and wished to submit a memorial exposing Yan's secret affairs, but because Yan remained at the center of power, he did not dare send it.
decisions.reason: Context shows 其陰事 are Zhufu Yan's secrets, not Zhao's; the proposal is right on reference but the parenthetical is awkward for a literal field.
